‘It Was Really Profound’: Chris Pratt Reveals Powerful Spiritual Experience While Filming Christian Film Pétros Ení

‘The idea that St. Peter is there is meaningful’

Actual Article Body:
Photo by Mike Coppola/Getty Images

Chris Pratt revealed he felt a powerful connection to his faith while filming his upcoming documentary, “Pétros Ení - Discovering the Origins.”

During a recent interview with Variety, the actor explained that IMAX drone cameras were used for his new Vatican documentary with Pope Leo. The cameras explored the tomb of St. Peter, in what Pratt described as a “profound” experience that redefined his Catholic faith.

Chris Pratt says Imax drone cameras were used for his new Vatican documentary with Pope Leo, which explores the tomb of St. Peter. He says the experience helped redefine his Catholic faith: “It was really profound to be encountering the remains of one of Jesus’ apostles. There was prophetic word, he said that the church will be built upon that rock. And Simon Peter is the rock. To see the church some 2,000 years later, and see the prophecy of his words came true, it just was really meaningful to me.”

“I think the idea that St. Peter is there is meaningful — and I don’t have time to fully dive into it in a quick interview like this — but I’d love to talk to you about it at some point,” Pratt told reporters in a social media clip shared Oct. 20 by Variety.

“It was really profound to be encountering the remains of one of Jesus’ apostles,” he said.

Pratt continued, “It was a prophetic word; he said that the church will be built upon that rock. And Simon Peter is the rock.”

The famous actor described the personal impact of the experience.

“To be there, and to see the church some 2,000 years later, and see the prophecy of his words come true, it just was really meaningful to me,” he told Variety.

Apple TV Press Day

SANTA MONICA, CALIFORNIA - FEBRUARY 03: Chris Pratt, from Apple’s film “Way of the Warrior Kid,” at the Apple TV Press Day at the Barker Hangar on February 03, 2026 in Santa Monica, California. The star-studded event highlighted a stellar lineup of original series and films coming to Apple TV in 2026. (Photo by JC Olivera/Apple TV via Getty Images)

“Pétros Ení” is a deep dive into the archaeological discoveries of St. Peter at the Vatican, and takes audiences on a journey grounded in faith and history at one of Christianity’s most significant sites.

“It was an incredible honor to collaborate with Pope Leo and the Vatican on this project,” Pratt said.

He continued, “The story of St. Peter is foundational to the Christian faith, and I am deeply grateful for the trust and access I was given to bring his legacy to the screen.” (RELATED: Dylan Sprouse Says He And Twin Cole Are Children Of Incest)

The documentary is slated for international theatrical release in February 2027.
